#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from Slurm
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 10 -g 1 -t 14d --job-name=sim3c --output=/hits/basement/nlp/fatimamh/outputs/hipo/exp03/out-{{id}} --error=/hits/basement/nlp/fatimamh/outputs/hipo/exp03/err-{{id}} script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (implicit from --ntasks=1)
# -n 1         : 1 task (from --ntasks=1)
# -c 10        : 10 cores per task (from --cpus-per-task=10)
# -g 1         : 1 GPU (from --gres=gpu:1)
# -t 14d       : 14 day walltime (from --time=14-00:00:00)
# --job-name=sim3c : job name (from --job-name=sim3c)
# --output=/hits/basement/nlp/fatimamh/outputs/hipo/exp03/out-{{id}} : output file with job ID
# --error=/hits/basement/nlp/fatimamh/outputs/hipo/exp03/err-{{id}} : error file with job ID
#
# Note: Flux uses {{id}} or {{jobid}} for job ID instead of %j
# Note: Flux time format uses d for days (14d = 14 days)

# Original job name: sim3c
# Set at submission: flux batch --job-name=sim3c ...

# Original output/error files:
# Slurm: /hits/basement/nlp/fatimamh/outputs/hipo/exp03/out-%j
# Slurm: /hits/basement/nlp/fatimamh/outputs/hipo/exp03/err-%j
# Flux: /hits/basement/nlp/fatimamh/outputs/hipo/exp03/out-{{id}}
# Flux: /hits/basement/nlp/fatimamh/outputs/hipo/exp03/err-{{id}}
# Set at submission with job ID placeholder

# Partition: pascal-deep.p
# Slurm: --partition=pascal-deep.p
# Note: Flux does not have partitions in the same way as Slurm
# Partition selection is handled through Flux's scheduling configuration
# Performance impact: Job scheduling depends on site-specific Flux configuration
# The 'pascal-deep.p' partition likely refers to nodes with Pascal GPU architecture
# Without partition specification, job may be scheduled on any available nodes
# For GPU architecture constraints, consult site-specific Flux configuration
# May need to use --requires or --setattr for GPU type constraints
# Example: --requires="gpu_model=pascal" (if configured in Flux resource graph)

# GPU allocation: 1 GPU
# Slurm: --gres=gpu:1
# Flux: -g 1 allocates 1 GPU
# Note: GPU type/model cannot be specified in standard Flux syntax
# The pascal-deep.p partition likely ensured Pascal architecture GPUs
# Performance impact: Job may be allocated different GPU types
# Consult site-specific Flux configuration for GPU property constraints

# Cores per task: 10
# Slurm: --cpus-per-task=10
# Flux: -c 10 specifies 10 cores per task
# This ensures the task has 10 CPU cores available

# Tasks: 1
# Slurm: --ntasks=1
# Flux: -n 1 specifies 1 task
# Single task execution (not MPI parallel)

# Walltime: 14 days
# Slurm: --time=14-00:00:00 (14 days, 0 hours, 0 minutes, 0 seconds)
# Flux: -t 14d (14 days)
# Note: Flux accepts time formats: #d (days), #h (hours), #m (minutes), #s (seconds)
# Or combined: #d#h#m#s

# Module load
module load CUDA/10.0.130

# Conda environment setup
. /home/fatimamh/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate kis

# Execute Python script
# Direct execution without flux run since this is a single-task job
# The task already has all allocated resources (10 cores, 1 GPU)
python /hits/basement/nlp/fatimamh/codes/keep_it_simple/run_keep_it_simple.py \
  -d /hits/basement/nlp/fatimamh/outputs/hipo/exp03/wiki_mono_test-rand_200-cos-edge-add_f=0.0_b=1.0_s=0.5

# Note on execution:
# For single-task jobs, direct python execution is appropriate
# Flux will ensure the task runs with allocated resources (10 cores, 1 GPU)
# If multi-task parallelization is needed in future, use:
# flux run -n <tasks> -c <cores-per-task> -g <gpus-per-task> python ...

# Complete submission command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 10 -g 1 -t 14d \
#   --job-name=sim3c \
#   --output=/hits/basement/nlp/fatimamh/outputs/hipo/exp03/out-{{id}} \
#   --error=/hits/basement/nlp/fatimamh/outputs/hipo/exp03/err-{{id}} \
#   script.sh

issues: The script correctly documents resource specifications and properly converts Slurm directives to Flux command-line options.

The output/error file placeholders use '{{id}}' which should be verified. Flux may use '{{id}}', '{{jobid}}', or '{id}' (single braces) depending on version. The double-brace syntax should be tested with the specific Flux installation.

The 14-day walltime is extremely long. Most HPC systems have maximum walltime limits (often 7 days or less). Verify that the Flux instance allows 14-day jobs, or consider implementing job checkpointing and chaining for robustness.

No memory specification is included. The original Slurm script also lacked memory specification, but for GPU workloads, explicit memory allocation is often beneficial. Consider adding '--setattr=system.memory=<value>' to the submission command based on application requirements.

The partition constraint (pascal-deep.p) for Pascal GPU architecture is documented but not translated to Flux syntax. If GPU architecture is critical, investigate site-specific Flux configuration for GPU property matching, possibly using '--requires' or '--setattr' options.

The script does not validate GPU availability or set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES explicitly. While Flux should handle GPU allocation, adding validation (e.g., 'nvidia-smi' check) before running the Python script would improve robustness.

The conda activation command does not check for success. Consider adding error handling: '. /home/fatimamh/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate kis || { echo "Conda activation failed"; exit 1; }'
The Python script execution does not capture exit status. Consider adding 'set -e' at the beginning of the script to exit on any error, or explicitly check the Python script's exit code.

The output directory path '/hits/basement/nlp/fatimamh/outputs/hipo/exp03/' is not validated. If the directory doesn't exist, the job will fail to write output files. Consider adding 'mkdir -p' for the output directory.
For a 14-day job, no checkpointing or intermediate output saving mechanism is mentioned. Consider implementing periodic checkpointing to avoid losing work if the job fails near completion.
